policy.rule: Evidence selects a defensible anchor band; the exact value inside that band must be justified by source-addressed facts and may not exceed what the evidence supports.
requirements: Every component value must be 0-100 and carry non-empty sourceIds plus a plain-language basis.
Issuer evidence may support a fact but does not count as independent corroboration of that same issuer claim.
Unknown or undisclosed facts reduce confidence; they are never silently treated as favorable.
A value outside the selected anchor band requires explicit contrary/exception evidence.
Calibration guidance never overrides Beast, causal, provenance, risk, confidence, T0 or publication gates.

thesisQuality.description: Durability of the problem, demonstrated product-market fit, defensible differentiation and credible value capture.

anchors.20: Problem or value capture is weak, temporary, substantially unproven or contradicted by primary evidence.
anchors.40: Real problem exists but adoption, differentiation or durable economics remain materially uncertain.
anchors.60: Credible problem and adoption with mixed evidence on moat, durability or value capture.
anchors.80: Strong primary evidence of durable demand, adoption, differentiation and economic capture.
anchors.100: Exceptional, repeatedly demonstrated problem durability and value capture with unusually difficult-to-copy advantages.

thesisQuality.policy: Evidence selects a defensible anchor band; the exact value inside that band must be justified by source-addressed facts and may not exceed what the evidence supports.

financialOperatingMomentum.description: Growth quality, margins/cash flow, demand visibility and balance-sheet ability to fund execution.

anchors.20: Deteriorating operations, weak liquidity or financing dependence threatens execution.
anchors.40: Mixed growth and cash generation with meaningful balance-sheet or execution pressure.
anchors.60: Adequate operating trend and funding capacity but material volatility or unresolved weaknesses remain.
anchors.80: Strong growth quality, margins/cash generation, demand visibility and funding capacity.
anchors.100: Exceptional broad-based operating acceleration with highly resilient funding and execution evidence.

financialOperatingMomentum.policy: Evidence selects a defensible anchor band; the exact value inside that band must be justified by source-addressed facts and may not exceed what the evidence supports.

marketValuationOpportunity.description: Valuation headroom, growth-adjusted valuation, asymmetry and dilution-adjusted per-share value.

anchors.20: Current valuation requires aggressive outcomes and offers poor downside-adjusted headroom.
anchors.40: Valuation is demanding relative to defensible growth or dilution-adjusted outcomes.
anchors.60: Roughly balanced valuation with plausible upside and downside.
anchors.80: Compelling valuation relative to well-supported growth and realistic dilution-adjusted scenarios.
anchors.100: Rare asymmetry where defensible value materially exceeds market expectations across several plausible scenarios.

marketValuationOpportunity.policy: Evidence selects a defensible anchor band; the exact value inside that band must be justified by source-addressed facts and may not exceed what the evidence supports.

catalystScore.description: Materiality, timing clarity, evidence quality and independence of identifiable catalysts.

anchors.20: Catalysts are speculative, immaterial, distant or unsupported.
anchors.40: Some catalysts exist but timing/materiality or evidence quality is weak.
anchors.60: At least one credible catalyst with moderate timing/evidence uncertainty.
anchors.80: Multiple material, source-supported catalysts with identifiable timing.
anchors.100: Several independent, near/medium-term catalysts capable of materially changing intrinsic value or thesis confidence.

catalystScore.policy: Evidence selects a defensible anchor band; the exact value inside that band must be justified by source-addressed facts and may not exceed what the evidence supports.

governancePower.description: Execution history, capital allocation, alignment, operator quality and transparency.

anchors.20: Material governance, credibility, control or capital-allocation defects are evidenced.
anchors.40: Governance is functional but important alignment, disclosure or execution concerns remain.
anchors.60: Generally adequate governance with mixed evidence on execution or capital allocation.
anchors.80: Strong execution history, aligned incentives, disciplined capital allocation and transparent disclosure.
anchors.100: Exceptional long-duration stewardship with repeated evidence of disciplined decisions and unusually strong alignment.

governancePower.policy: Evidence selects a defensible anchor band; the exact value inside that band must be justified by source-addressed facts and may not exceed what the evidence supports.

alignment2036.description: Exposure to durable human needs, critical infrastructure, long-duration technology tailwinds and strategic relevance.

anchors.20: Little durable connection to important future human/infrastructure needs or structurally declining relevance.
anchors.40: Some future relevance but dependent on narrow, uncertain or replaceable demand.
anchors.60: Credible exposure to at least one durable need or technology transition.
anchors.80: Strong multi-year exposure to critical human, industrial or infrastructure needs.
anchors.100: Foundational capability required across multiple plausible 2036 futures and difficult to replace.

anchors.40: Some diversification but major dependence on one market/customer/theme remains.
anchors.60: Several demand channels with moderate reuse/diversification.
anchors.80: Multiple independent demand engines reuse core capabilities efficiently across markets.
anchors.100: Exceptional platform leverage where several structurally independent markets reinforce the same core capability.

bottleneckControl.description: Scarcity, switching costs, capacity lead times and ownership of a real system constraint.

anchors.20: No demonstrated scarce capability or customers can replace supply relatively easily.
anchors.40: Some constraint exposure but limited control, modest switching costs or short capacity response.
anchors.60: Meaningful constraint participation with partial scarcity or switching-cost evidence.
anchors.80: Strong control of scarce capacity/capability with long lead times and material switching costs.
anchors.100: Company controls an exceptional, system-critical bottleneck with no practical near-term substitute.

scenarioRobustness.description: Ability to win across divergent futures through optionality, geographic diversity and adaptable business models.

anchors.20: Thesis depends on a narrow scenario and has little downside optionality.
anchors.40: Material exposure to one macro, technology, geography or customer outcome.
anchors.60: Can survive several scenarios but important concentration remains.
anchors.80: Strong economics/capabilities across multiple materially different plausible futures.
anchors.100: Exceptional anti-fragility or optionality where divergent scenarios create multiple credible paths to value.

anchors.40: Differentiation exists but cost/performance or technology substitution risk is substantial.
anchors.60: Moderate replacement barriers and a credible roadmap, with meaningful substitution threats remaining.
anchors.80: Strong performance/cost edge, qualification barriers and roadmap adaptability.
anchors.100: Exceptionally difficult to replace and positioned to own or absorb likely successor technologies.

anchors.40: Material concentration and long-lead exposure with limited redundancy.
anchors.60: Some redundancy and planning, but meaningful critical dependencies remain.
anchors.80: Demonstrated multi-source/geographic resilience with practical inventory/substitution/vertical-control paths.
anchors.100: Exceptionally resilient supply architecture with tested redundancy and multiple credible paths around critical constraints.

pricingPower.description: Observed margin durability, price pass-through, scarcity rent and contract structures that preserve economics.

anchors.20: Commodity-like pricing with weak margins and little ability to pass through costs.
anchors.40: Limited pricing flexibility; economics are sensitive to competition or input inflation.
anchors.60: Some demonstrated pricing power but not durable across cycles/customers.
anchors.80: Strong margin evidence, pass-through ability or scarcity rent supported by contracts/market structure.
anchors.100: Exceptional durable value capture with structurally protected pricing and scarce/mission-critical capability.

source-integrity.name: provenance
source-integrity.basis: SEC filing identity, issuer operating evidence and independent current valuation are source-addressed and origin-separated.

source-integrity.name: freshness
source-integrity.basis: Operating evidence is from the quarter ended June 30, 2026 and valuation is dated September 24, 2026.

source-integrity.name: sourceIndependence
source-integrity.basis: Operating facts remain issuer/SEC-derived; current valuation adds an independent market-data origin, while duplicated Q2 issuer lineage is explicitly collapsed.

company-underwriting.name: underwriting
company-underwriting.basis: Strong strategic positioning and improving operating conversion are balanced by demanding valuation and execution/policy dependence.

structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: Domestic mine-to-separated-product-to-magnet capability addresses multiple stages of a concentrated rare-earth supply chain.

structural-causal.name: supplyChainResilience
structural-causal.basis: Domestic downstream conversion can diversify strategic magnet supply if ramp and qualification succeed.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: Strategic demand is broad, while economics remain sensitive to ramp execution, policy support and rare-earth pricing.

structural-causal.name: substitutionResilience
structural-causal.basis: NdFeB magnets are performance-critical in many applications, but motor redesign, recycling and alternative magnet chemistries can reduce intensity in some uses.

discovery-weak-signals.name: domestic rare-earth vertical integration
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Rising separated-product output, magnetics revenue and new defense/offtake programs broaden evidence of downstream conversion.

adversarial-red-team.name: policyDependence
adversarial-red-team.basis: Government support can de-risk strategic capacity while obscuring unsupported market economics.

adversarial-red-team.name: executionConcentration
adversarial-red-team.basis: Multiple large ramp programs create correlated schedule and qualification exposure.

adversarial-red-team.name: confidenceInflation
adversarial-red-team.basis: Commercial milestones are real, but future 10X utilization and economics are not yet achieved facts.

expectations-execution.name: execution conversion
expectations-execution.basis: Commercial magnetics revenue/EBITDA and record-scale NdPr sales show tangible conversion while major capacity programs remain forward execution tests.
